title: Warm Spinach Chicken Salad
seoTitle: Warm Spinach Chicken Salad | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sliced chicken over wilted spinach with bacon vinaigrette for ten
subtitle: Sliced chicken over wilted spinach with bacon vinaigrette for ten
description: Chicken thighs roast and slice, then serve over lightly wilted spinach with warm bacon-mustard vinaigrette, sliced mushrooms, and hard-boiled egg. Hearty enough for a cold-night shift.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Warm Spinach Chicken Salad in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use hard-boiled eggs as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Season thighs with salt and olive oil. Roast at 425°F on a sheet pan 25–30 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest and slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Cook bacon and mushrooms
steps.instruction: Render bacon in a skillet until crisp. Remove and chop. Sauté mushrooms in bacon fat 6–8 minutes until golden. Set aside. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build warm vinaigrette
steps.instruction: Whisk vinegar, mustard, and shallot into warm bacon fat off heat. Crumble half the bacon into the dressing. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.instruction: Toss spinach in a large bowl with warm dressing until leaves just wilt—about 30 seconds of gentle tossing. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: portion and serve
steps.instruction: Top wilted spinach with sliced chicken, mushrooms, egg quarters, and remaining bacon crumbles. Serve immediately. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Baby spinach handles warm dressing better than mature spinach leaves.
Add sliced red grapes for sweet contrast if your crew likes fruit in salad.
This does not hold—plate to order or assemble in small batches.
tonightSpread: Warm spinach salad plated with crusty rolls on the side.
Roasted sweet potato wedges for crew who want more carbs.
leftovers: Slice cold chicken for sandwiches with leftover bacon.
Use wilted spinach in a frittata the next morning.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Warm salad sounds fancy but it is just smart hall cooking—hot dressing wilts spinach slightly and makes the plate feel like dinner, not diet food.
mealPrepNotes: Render bacon slowly for best vinaigrette fat. Dress spinach lightly at service—too much and it collapses. Mushrooms sauté just before plating.
